title: Faces of the sangha
hook: wise, powerful, forgetful, proud, gentle: all were welcome

segments.voice: Yesterday, even Devadatta, named in the Lotus Sutra as the Buddha's past teacher and promised buddhahood. Your line was even him. Did you wish one good thing to someone who crossed you? Day seven hundred seventy-nine.

Line them up the way the texts remember them. A man the texts call foremost in wisdom. His friend, foremost in powers. A slow monk who couldn't keep a single verse in his head. A former charioteer too proud to take advice from anyone. A cousin so gentle he served as attendant, bringing water and keeping the door. Different speeds, different tempers, different flaws, all in one robe color. None of them was turned away for being who he was. Today, the faces of the sangha.

First, the word. Sangha means community, an assembly. In the narrow sense it's the order of monks and nuns. In a wider sense, some Buddhists use it for everyone who walks the path together. It's the third of the Three Jewels, beside the Buddha and the dhamma, the things a Buddhist goes to for refuge. Second, the wise and the powerful. Sariputta and Moggallana, the two chief disciples, are the faces people expect. The texts praise one for wisdom and the other for power, and the path has met both. Third, the slow and the proud. In a commentary story, Culapanthaka's own brother told him to leave the order, because he couldn't learn one verse. The Buddha handed him a clean white cloth instead, and as he rubbed it gray, he understood. And Channa, the former charioteer, was so stubborn that the Buddha, before he died, said the monks should give him the higher penalty: no one would speak to him or advise him. The Vinaya says that silence brought him to his senses, and he too awakened. Fourth, the same path at different paces. Ananda, gentle and loyal, was still not awakened when the Buddha died. The sangha was never a gallery of finished people. It was a room where people at very different points sat side by side. And the welcome had a shape. It wasn't approval of every flaw. Channa's pride was met with a hard silence. But the silence was meant to bring him back, not to push him out.
screen: `SANGHA: THE COMMUNITY.` · `WISE AND POWERFUL, SIDE BY SIDE.` · `SLOW AND PROUD, STILL WELCOME.` · `ONE PATH, DIFFERENT PACES.` · then, large: `ALL WERE WELCOME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: accept one flaw in a friend. Settle, and let the breath find its own pace. Bring one friend to mind. Let one of their flaws come up, the habit that wears on you. Running late. Talking over people. Forgetting things you told them. Don't fix it. Don't excuse it, either. Just set it beside everything else they are, the way the sangha set the slow monk beside the wise one. The flaw is real, and the friend is more than the flaw. Rest there for a few breaths. The bell holds the time.
Faces of the sangha. Wise, powerful, forgetful, proud, gentle: one community that made room for all of them. Today's word.
Your line: all were welcome. Today, when that friend's flaw shows up, let it pass once without a comment, and notice what else they bring. Day seven hundred seventy-nine.

howItsDone: Buddhists go for refuge to the Buddha, the dhamma and the sangha, often reciting the three refuges in Pali at the start of a gathering, and teachers retell the disciples' stories to show that people of every temperament walked the path.

match.prompt: faces of the sangha: tap the pairs.
pairs: not yet awake when the Buddha died

myth: only the wisest disciples were allowed to stay
a slow monk, a proud charioteer and a gentle attendant all stayed, each at his own pace.
Channa's pride was met with silence from the community
before he died the Buddha said the monks should give Channa the higher penalty: no one would speak to him or advise him.
the sangha is the third of the Three Jewels
Buddha, dhamma and sangha: the three refuges.

fork.setup: the Buddha has died, and Ananda, his gentle attendant, is still not awakened. where does that leave him?
options: outside the sangha until he awakens.
still in the sangha, at his own pace.
leading the sangha in the Buddha's place.
fork.reveal: the sangha was never a gallery of finished people. Ananda sat beside the awakened, walking the same path at a different pace.

original.note: Pali saṅgha: community, assembly. The third of the Three Jewels.

trapdoor: what you thought: the sangha was a gathering of saints.
what it means: wise, powerful, slow, proud and gentle people walked the same path at different paces.
what a scholar hears: sangha can mean the order of monks and nuns, the noble sangha of those who have reached the paths, or, in wider modern use, a whole community of practitioners.

sources.ref: DN 16, Mahaparinibbana Sutta (the higher penalty for Channa)
Vinaya, Cullavagga 11 (Channa receives the higher penalty and later awakens)
Dhammapada commentary on verse 25 (Culapanthaka and the white cloth)
AN 1 (the chapter of the foremost: Sariputta in wisdom, Moggallana in psychic power)

notes: This is a looking-back day: Sariputta (728, 730), Moggallana (729), Culapanthaka (772), Channa (752) and Ananda (732–738) were taught earlier; check that the summaries match those days' scripts.

Channa: DN 16 has the Buddha prescribe the brahmadanda; Cullavagga 11 tells how Ananda delivers it and Channa, distressed, later becomes an arahant. 'That silence brought him to his senses' is a paraphrase; confirm.
Culapanthaka: 'his own brother told him to leave' follows the Dhammapada commentary (Mahapanthaka); confirm.
howItsDone: 'often reciting the three refuges in Pali at the start of a gathering' describes common Theravada practice; confirm phrasing for a pan-Buddhist path.

Editor pass: cut unsourced 'stayed humble' (Moggallana); 'old charioteer' to 'former charioteer'; Ananda 'spent his life' to 'served as attendant'; 'Buddhists use' to 'some Buddhists use'; fork replaced (it repeated day 772's Culapanthaka-at-the-gate fork) with an Ananda item from today's teach.

Audit: hook's 'wise' figure described as one who 'could unfold in detail what the Buddha said in a sentence', which is Mahakaccana's etadagga (day 775), not Sariputta's; rewritten to 'foremost in wisdom' (AN 1) so it matches the teach. Teach's leftover 'old charioteer' changed to 'former charioteer'.
